tips.li: Food poisoning comes from two places: a clumsy cook and a dirty kitchen. A skilled cook rarely poisons anyone; a kitchen below -2 cleanliness makes even good cooks dangerous.
Nutrient paste never causes food poisoning. Raw food can.
Butchering sprays blood and drags the room's cleanliness down. Give the butcher table its own room next door, not a corner of the kitchen.
Floors matter in a kitchen. Bare ground collects filth; tiles are easy to keep clean, and sterile tiles are the best of all.
Once a cook reaches Cooking 6 and you have both meat and vegetables, fine meals cost no more food than simple ones and lift everyone's mood.
A butcher table counts as -15 cleanliness on its own tile, and every spatter of blood is another -10.
Cleaning only happens inside the Home area, and only by colonists who have Cleaning switched on in the Work tab.
A dirty hospital raises the chance of infection and botched surgery. Keep it clean before you need it.
Entrances collect dirt from boots. A doormat of hard floor near the door and a dedicated cleaner keep it under control.
Blood is -10 cleanliness per tile, vomit -15, ordinary filth -5. One fight in the hospital undoes a day of sweeping.
Wood is quick to build with and quick to burn. Put stone walls around anything that holds a flame: campfires, torches, stoves, heaters.
Fire spreads across wooden floors and through stockpiles of cloth and wood. Store flammables in a separate stone room.
Keep a firefighter on high priority and the Home area covering your buildings: colonists only fight fires inside it.
Batteries can short-circuit and set rooms alight, especially when rain gets in. Keep them under a roof, away from anything that burns.
Short circuits come from ordinary power conduits and unroofed batteries. Hidden conduits and roofed batteries can't short out.
Hives can only appear under overhead mountain, warmer than -17 °C and within 30 tiles of your buildings. They prefer dark spots far from open sky.
Only walls stop hives from spawning, not doors or columns. Walling up every second tile of an unused mountain room is enough.
Keeping a mountain room at or below -17 °C keeps insects out of it entirely.
Fire works on insects too: they hate it, and so will your walls if they're wooden.
Seeing a body, fresh or rotting, ruins a colonist's mood. Rotting ones are worse and smell for days.
A dumping stockpile far from the base, set to accept corpses, keeps the dead out of sight until you can bury or burn them.
Colonists who died deserve graves. Friends and family carry that grief until they're laid to rest.
Seeing a body costs 4 mood, a rotting one 6, and it happens again every time someone walks past.
Blight spreads to nearby crops. Cut blighted plants at once, and break huge fields into smaller ones with gaps between them.
Frost kills crops. When the cold comes, harvest everything that's ripe enough rather than gambling on another week.
Rich soil is the best farmland on most maps. Don't build on it.
Plants rest at night, so real growing time is close to twice what the crop's info card says.
Leave about 4 tiles between fields: blight jumps up to 4 tiles from plant to plant.
Raiders love setting fields alight. Keep wild brush and piles of wood a couple of tiles away from crops.
A poor colony is easily pleased. As wealth grows, everyone expects more, and the free mood bonus from low expectations shrinks step by step.
Higher expectations also mean colonists need more kinds of recreation and tire of the same fun faster.
Wealth also decides how big raids get. Hoarding silver and art you don't use is a double cost.
Expectations by colony wealth: +30 mood below 15,000, +24 below 31,000, +18 below 81,000, +12 below 182,000, +6 below 308,000, and nothing above.
Wardens feed, talk to and recruit prisoners. Without one, prisoners go hungry and recruitment stalls.
Every door into a prison cell is another chance for a breakout. One cell, one door, solid walls.
Happy, well-fed prisoners are easier to recruit. A decent cell costs little and saves a lot of beatings later.
Prisoners can only be recruited once their resistance reaches 0. A warden they like and a prisoner in a good mood wear it down much faster.
Executing a guilty prisoner costs your colonists a little mood; an innocent one costs more.
Colonists in the dark get a mood penalty and work more slowly. Every room people use at night needs a light.
Torches and lamps on walls save floor space, and one good light covers a fair-sized room.
Surgery under a dim light is less likely to succeed. Light the hospital before you need it.
Most weather disasters end. Stay indoors, keep the food cold and the colonists warm, and wait it out.
A restricted area that keeps everyone under a roof is the fastest way to protect them from toxic fallout.
A solar flare lasts 0.15 to 0.5 days. A heat wave or cold snap lasts 1.5 to 3.5 days. None of them lasts forever.
